checks: Every side length is affine and positive, so the real boxes are exactly the Minkowski interpolants of the endpoint boxes. Therefore the hull of the mixed intersection equals the entire body.
The two endpoint volumes agree because A/(2+A)=s^(d−1) and B/(2+B)=s. The affine dependence of the box centroids on z identifies the original mixed centroid and places it in the central fiber.
Substituting t=1−z+B changes the integrand to (2+A+B−t)t^(d−1) on [B,2+B]. Its antiderivative gives the stated expression and the s→0 limit 2^(d+1)/(d(d+1)) while M_s→1.

The limit diverges as d increases, and continuity after choosing a finite d gives a strictly positive rational s that realizes each strict bound. Source bf1136671db3fa6d has the same exact hull, centroid and ratio.

overlap.comparison: Its volume comparison concerns fixed continuous dimension two and additional projection regimes. It does not yield a dimension-independent ambient-to-mixed volume bound on these canonical hulls.

summary: The exact canonical hull has three positive integer fibers and its true centroid at the middle box center, while its ambient-to-mixed volume ratio is unbounded as continuous dimension varies.
